sections.heading: When to use
sections.text: Use Vienna rectifier for three-phase unidirectional PFC. Only three active switches (vs six in conventional bridge), inherent three-level modulation reduces input current THD, no shoot-through risk. THD < 5% achievable with proper current-loop bandwidth.

sections.heading: Controller structure
sections.text: Control in dq frame with inner current loop and outer voltage loop. Neutral-point voltage balance is an additional control loop that adjusts the common-mode duty-cycle offset. The voltage loop bandwidth must stay below 2*f_line (typically 10-20 Hz).

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: Unidirectional power flow only (boost mode). Neutral-point voltage balancing is required — if the split capacitors have unequal voltage, the output current waveform distorts. The neutral-point balancing loop should be 5-10x faster than the voltage loop.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If THD is high, increase current-loop bandwidth. If the neutral-point voltage oscillates, increase the balancing loop gain. If the output voltage oscillates at 6*f_line, reduce the voltage-loop bandwidth below 2*f_line.
